name: envy
quote: I'd like hair as nice as hers.
description: A desire for a characteristic or asset belonging to someone else along with the sense that it would be possible, but difficult, to achieve.
perceptions: That person has a characteristic or asset that I would like to have.
It would be possible, but it would be a lot of effort and luck.
results: You may quickly forget about the desire, become fixated on it, or perhaps become motivated to achieve it for yourself.
examples: Wanting to be as stylish as your brother.
Wanting to have the kind of relationship your roommate has.

guidance.description: Envious feelings can eat you up, but it doesn’t have to be that way. Here’s how to transform envy into a guide and motivator.

variations.name: shameful envy
variations.description: A desire for a characteristic or asset belonging to someone else along with the sense that others might consider this desire negatively.
perceptions: That person has a characteristic or asset that I would like to have.
If others knew I wanted it, they would think negatively of me.
examples: A doctor envious of another doctor's breakthrough internally downplaying its importance.

variations.name: guilty envy
variations.description: A desire for a characteristic or asset belonging to someone else along with a dissonant regret for wanting it.
perceptions: That person has a characteristic or asset that I would like to have.
But I should be happy for them.
I should be satisfied with what I have.
It's not appropriate for me to want their thing.
examples: A work friend gets a deserved promotion and you think it could have been you.

commentaries.quote: Envy is the ulcer of the soul.
Envy comes from people's ignorance of, or lack of belief in, their own gifts.
Our envy always lasts longer than the happiness of those we envy.
Few men have the natural strength to honor a friend’s success without envy.
Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's goods.
